newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudanese militia says takes town from rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese militia says takes town from rebels.

text.p: The head of a pro-government militia in southern Sudan said his forces have recaptured the town of Litnom in Bahr al-Ghazal province from the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
The government newspaper al-Anbaa on Sunday quoted Kerubino Kwanyin Bol, leader of the SPLA-Bahr al-Ghazal group, as saying the town fell to his forces on Thursday.

Bol's group broke with the mainstream SPLA of Colonel John Garang several years ago and signed a peace agreement with the government in April. Garang refused to sign, saying the Islamist government in Khartoum was not serious about peace.
Bol said his forces killed 94 of Garang's men in the fighting for Litnom, for the loss of 17 of his own men.
The SPLA seized several towns in the Bahr al-Ghazal area in an offensive earlier this year but it did not name Litnom.
The same government newspaper said that Garang's nephew, named as James Atem, was killed earlier this month by mutinous soldiers in the SPLA unit he commanded.
It said the soldiers killed Atem on Fanjak island in Upper Nile province when Atem came to inspect them. The unit had defected to the pro-government militia led by Riek Machar.
SPLA officials were not immediately available to comment on the two reports. Sudanese government newspapers have often prematurely reported the death of leading SPLA members.
